# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)</sub>
- **Status:** Widow  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P1](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0001)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>; Aunty J.  <sub>[v3 c24 P5](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

She is a tiny old woman with a softly-triangular face, pink cheeks, and large, soft blue eyes filled with youth. Her hair is snow-white and styled in quaint little puffs over her ears. She dresses in an old-fashioned manner.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina has a youthful, cheerful spirit combined with old-fashioned views and opinions. She is warm-hearted, loving, and tolerant, believing in letting young people enjoy their freedom while retaining a proper respect for religion and duty. She possesses a lively sense of humor and enjoys joking about suitors and past experiences.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P64](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0064), [v3 c19 P1](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0001), [v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004), [v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)_

## Traits

- Sweet and good-hearted  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c19 P37](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0037)</sub>
- Old-fashioned  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>
- Tolerant and forgiving  <sub>[v3 c16 P64](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0064), [v3 c35 P17](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0017)</sub>
- Horror of snakes  <sub>[v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)</sub>

## Abilities

- Knitting  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c25 P2](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0002)</sub>
- Housekeeping and managing a home  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P1](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0001)</sub>

## Goals

- To keep house for the college girls at Patty's Place  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- To get a yellow silk dress in heaven  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>

## History

After her daughter married and left for the foreign mission field, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house. Her relative Stella suggested she move to Kingsport to keep house at Patty's Place for Stella, Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon during their studies at Redmond College. She moved into Patty's Place bringing two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, and eventually adopted Rusty as well. She kept house for the girls throughout their remaining college years, providing warm support and practical wisdom. After the students graduated and scattered, she traveled to India to explore her daughter's mission field.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P55](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0055), [v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058), [v3 c38 P8](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0008), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)_

## Background by volume

- Named after her father James, who drowned at sea prior to her birth  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- Her late husband refused to let her wear a yellow silk dress  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>
- Her daughter Elizabeth earned an M.A. and became a missionary  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c27 P6](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0006), [v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)</sub>

## Quotes

> My clothes are, and it stands to reason my opinions are, too. I don’t say they’re any the better of that, mind you. In fact, I daresay they’re a good deal the worse. But they’ve worn nice and easy.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> Do your duty by God and your neighbor and yourself, and have a good time. That’s my philosophy and it’s always worked pretty well.  <sub>[v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004)</sub>

> The very first thing I’m going to do when I get to heaven is to get a yellow silk dress.  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>

> Never mind. Thank goodness air and salvation are still free  <sub>[v3 c17 P4](../source/v03-c17.md#nw-v03-c17-p0004)</sub>

> People who haven’t natural gumption never learn, neither in college nor life. If they live to be a hundred they really don’t know anything more than when they were born.  <sub>[v3 c37 P26](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0026)</sub>
